items.body:
**Alternative to #5412.** Same problem, imperative API instead of the prop trio. Opened for comparison — these are mutually exclusive; only one should land.

## Problem

`value` holds a parsed number, so it can't represent text that isn't a number yet. Typing `-1.5` passes through `-` and `-1.`, neither of which parses, and both leave `value` untouched. Those are legal states internally — typing `-` already leaves the text as `-` with `value` at `null` — but there was no way to reach them programmatically.

## Solution

Adds `actionsRef` with a `setInputValue` action, following the pattern `Popover.Root` already uses.

```tsx
const actionsRef = React.useRef<NumberField.Root.Actions | null>(null);

<NumberField.Root min={-100} actionsRef={actionsRef}>

actionsRef.current.setInputValue('-');
```

The action mirrors what typing the same string does, minus the per-character gating that exists to reject keystrokes — the caller chose the string deliberately. `value` follows the text when it parses, is left alone when it doesn't (so `'-'` can sit over an existing number without clearing it), and an empty string clears it. Changes report `reason: 'imperative-action'`.

## Comparison with #5412

|  | This PR | #5412 (prop trio) |
|---|---|---|
| Diff | +249 / −5, 1 file of source (+52) | +1267 / −114, 6 files of source (+357 / −79) |
| New state | none | `useControlled` text, authorship tracking, write dedupe |
| Reading the current text | `state.inputValue` only | same, plus `onInputValueChange` |
| Observing text changes | not possible | every change, with a reason |
| Vetoing a change | not possible | `eventDetails.cancel()` |
| Driving from a reducer / form library | no | yes |
| Text is | ordinary component state | controllable |

The imperative version is much smaller because it reuses the dirty-text machinery that already exists for typing, rather than making the text a controllable value.

The cost is that the caller can't observe or negotiate. Text set this way behaves as an unsaved edit: it survives re-renders and external `value` changes with no callback to say so, and the field reclaims the display on the next value-changing interaction. `should survive a later external value change until an interaction reconciles it` pins that, including the fact that blur does *not* reclaim it when the text can't parse — the field goes on showing something its value contradicts until an interaction resolves it.

That last part is a pre-existing quirk on `master`, not introduced here. #5412 fixes it as part of its refactor; this PR leaves it in place, which is the honest cost of the smaller diff.

## Testing

9 new tests covering the intermediate-string cases, value coupling, the reason, and the reconciliation behavior above.

Full jsdom suite (7513) green, 400 jsdom / 430 chromium NumberField tests, forced `tsgo -b` clean, plus eslint, stylelint, prettier, `valelint`, and an idempotent `docs:validate`.

items.title: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
`Field.Control` was the only Field control that ignored controlled value changes. Switch, Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Radio Group, Select, Slider, Combobox, Number Field, and OTP Field all sync through `useValueChanged` already. `Field.Control` instead drove every field concern from the DOM change event, so a value set from code had no path at all.

Two bugs followed.

**Dirty state never cleared for non-string values.** The dirty check compares the input's string value against a baseline captured from the `value` prop. With `value={5}` the baseline was the number `5`, so `"5" !== 5` held forever and `data-dirty` stayed set even after the user returned the field to its initial value. Array values failed the same way by reference. The control now registers the serialized value, so the baseline and the comparison agree.

**Programmatic changes left the field stale.** Setting the value from code, such as a clear button or a form library reset, updated the input text but not filled, dirty, or validity, so a resolved error stayed visible and a pending async validator for the old value could still publish.

The fix gives each mode one owner instead of running two sync paths at once. `useValueChanged` owns the controlled path, `onChange` owns the uncontrolled path, and `onChange` returns early when controlled. `Field.Control` now has the same shape as its siblings, with the residual difference being the mount-time DOM read that its uncontrolled mode requires.

Two smaller fixes ride along:

- `details.cancel()` in `onValueChange` now stops the internal handling. It was ignored.
- A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field.

## Performance

Renders per keystroke for a controlled input, counted in jsdom (mount, then four keystrokes):

| Validation mode | Base | This PR | Number Field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSubmit` | 1 per keystroke | 2 on the first, then 1 | 2 on the first, then 1 |
| `onChange` | 1 per keystroke | 2 per keystroke | 2 per keystroke |

Moving the work into a layout effect costs one extra render per keystroke in `onChange` mode. That is the cost every sibling control already pays, and `Field.Control` now matches Number Field exactly. The base column achieved one render by doing the work synchronously in the change handler, which is the second sync path this PR removes.

items.title: [number field] Preserve numeric precision while keeping default display formatting

labels.name: component: number field
labels.description: Changes related to the number field component.

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: A bug, but worse, it used to behave as expected.

items.body:
- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

Fixes precision loss in the NumberField numeric pipeline while keeping the existing default display formatting. This is a compatibility-preserving fix: visible text still follows `Intl.NumberFormat` defaults (e.g. `1.235` for a no-format field), while the stored numeric value no longer loses precision when stepping or on blur.

## What was wrong

`removeFloatingPointErrors` rounded the stored numeric value to 3 fraction digits whenever `format` had no Intl rounding options. The 3-digit default was accidental: the original code intended a full-precision fallback (`... ?? defaultOptions.maximumFractionDigits ?? 20`), but `new Intl.NumberFormat().resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` is `3`, so the `?? 20` never applied.

Consequences:

- `step` / `smallStep` finer than `0.001` were silent no-ops at the numeric level: incrementing from `0` by `0.0001` rounded back to `0`, so `onValueChange` never fired and the value never advanced. Native `<input type="number" step="0.0001">` works fine.
- Button increment/decrement always parsed the visible (rounded) input text before stepping, so a value like `1.23456` — displayed as `1.235` — advanced from the rounded `1.235`, dropping precision even when the input wasn't dirty.
- Blur re-parsed the rounded display text and committed it, so a focus/blur with no edits (or a blur after a programmatic change) collapsed the stored value to its displayed precision.

## What changed

**Numeric pipeline keeps precision (display unchanged)**

- Floating-point cleanup is now noise-only for no-format arithmetic. The no-rounding branch of `removeFloatingPointErrors` cleans binary noise (`0.1 + 0.2` → `0.3`) via `toPrecision(15)`, but only when the correction is within a capped epsilon (`min(Number.EPSILON * max(1, |value|), 1e-10)`). The cap stops `toPrecision(15)` from corrupting large fractional values and high-significance step values — e.g. `100000000000000.1 + 0.1`, `0.1234567890123456`, and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned verbatim because their delta exceeds the cap.
- Parsed input (typing, paste, blur) carries no arithmetic noise, so `toValidatedNumber` returns it verbatim when there is no step and no rounding format — keeping every typed digit, including values beyond 15 significant digits.
- This fixes `step` / `smallStep` finer than `0.001` at the numeric value level: the value now advances and `onValueChange` fires, even though the visible text still rounds per Intl defaults.

**Interactions read numeric state, not rounded display**

- Button increment/decrement: `useNumberFieldButton`'s `commitValue` now parses `inputValue` before stepping only when the input is dirty and uncommitted (`!allowInputSyncRef.current`). When the input is already synced, it steps from the numeric state instead of the rounded visible text.
- Keyboard `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`: same authority rule — parse `inputValue` only when the input has unsaved edits; otherwise step from the numeric state (`valueRef`). Previously the keyboard path always parsed the rounded display, so a synced field collapsed precision (e.g. `1.23456` → `2.235` instead of `2.23456`). Wheel and scrub already stepped from numeric state.
- Input blur: when the input wasn't manually edited and there are no rounding options, blur commits the stored numeric value as-is instead of re-parsing the rounded display text. A no-edit focus/blur, or a blur after a programmatic change, no longer discards precision. (With explicit rounding options, blur still rounds the committed value to the format.)

**Display formatting unchanged (compatibility-preserving)**

- The blur handler and controlled-value sync always format visible text with the default `formatNumber` path (the max-precision display path is removed). Visible text follows `Intl.NumberFormat` defaults exactly as before — no full-precision display by default.
- Explicit Intl rounding options from #4804 (`roundingMode`, significant digits, `roundingIncrement`, percent display-scale rounding on blur) are still respected; that branch is unchanged.

## Behavior (no `format`, value `1.23456`)

| Action | Displayed text | Numeric value (`onValueChange` / `onValueCommitted`) |
|---|---|---|
| type `1.23456`, then blur | `1.235` (Intl default) | `1.23456` |
| re-focus + blur with no edit | `1.235` (unchanged) | `1.23456` (unchanged, no commit) |
| increment `+1` (button or `ArrowUp`) | `2.235` (Intl default) | `2.23456` |
| `step={0.0001}` from `0` | `0` (Intl default) | advances `0.0001`, `0.0002`, … (was a silent no-op) |

Visible text matches the pre-regression default formatting; only the numeric value pipeline is corrected so precision is no longer lost.

## Tests

- Reframed the tests that asserted the accidental 3-digit numeric default or the max-precision display: they now assert default-formatted display text alongside full-precision numeric values.
- Added regression tests:
  - stepping from numeric state rather than rounded display text — buttons (uncontrolled `defaultValue`, and after typed precision is formatted on blur) and keyboard `ArrowUp` (synced `defaultValue`, and after a no-edit blur cycle);
  - a no-edit focus/blur cycle keeping full numeric precision, including subsequent stepping;
  - a canceled synced button step not committing a stale value after an external change;
  - sub-`0.001` `step` / `smallStep` advancing the numeric value and firing `onValueChange`;
  - `removeFloatingPointErrors` unit tests for noise cleanup (incl. negative), the capped epsilon (large fractional, high-significance step, safe-integer exactness), and verbatim parsed input beyond 15 significant digits.

items.body:
# Feature request

## Summary

The `Form` component supports a native submit button - `<button type="submit">` - but not a reset button:

```jsx
<Form onSubmit={() => console.log('submitted')}>
   <Field.Root>
     {/*  a normal Field.Control that renders an input */}
   </Field.Root>

   {/* works */}
   <button type="submit">
     Submit
   </button>

   {/* doesn't work */}
   <button type="reset">
     Reset
   </button>
</Form>
```

## Examples in other libraries

- [React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Form.html#events) provides a reset button `<Form><Button type="reset" /></Form>`
- [React Hook Form](https://www.react-hook-form.com/faqs/#Howtoresettheform) supports a native reset button and also a `reset()` method via a hook

## Motivation

It's often useful to be able to discard all edits in a form and reset it to the initial values. This will could require Fields to additionally track the `initialValue`.

labels.description: It’s an improvement, but we can’t make up our mind whether it's a bug fix or a new feature.

items.body:
# Feature request

## Summary

I'm using the NumberField component as a quantity input in a shopping cart.
To avoid sending too many HTTP requests, I use a debounce of 200ms on value change.

## Examples in other libraries

<!-- Provide a link to examples of this component or feature implemented in other libraries (if applicable).  -->

## Motivation

Problem:
The component’s built-in `START_AUTO_CHANGE_DELAY` is fixed at 400ms.
So when a user holds down the increment button:

At 200ms: debounce triggers an HTTP request (from the initial increment)

At 400ms: auto-repeat starts, causing a second value change → another HTTP request

This leads to two requests even though the user only held the button once.

Proposal:
Allow START_AUTO_CHANGE_DELAY to be set via props, so it can be aligned with external debounce timing.

Example API:


```tsx
<NumberField startAutoChangeDelay={200} />
```

Current Workaround:
Set the debounce timeout to >= 400ms, however this introduces a less responsive UX and feels laggy.

labels.name: component: select

labels.name: type: bug

items.body:
In a multiple Select inside a Field, `[data-dirty]` stayed set after the selection returned to its initial value.

## Root cause

The dirty check used `value !== validityData.initialValue`. In multiple mode `value` is a fresh array on every change, so the reference comparison was always true once the user interacted — even after deselecting and reselecting back to the initial items.

## Changes

- Compare array values element-by-element via `isItemEqualToValue` when computing dirty state in multiple mode, falling back to reference comparison for non-array values. This mirrors the equivalent combobox fix.
- Add regression tests for returning to the initial value, object values compared via `isItemEqualToValue`, and the order-sensitive case.

## Notes

- The comparison is order-sensitive, matching `CheckboxGroup` and `Slider`. Returning to the same items in a different order is still treated as dirty.

items.title: [utils] Enforce store state key/value types

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

labels.name: package: utils
labels.description: Specific to the utils package.

items.body:
> [!Tip]
> Easier to review with [hidden whitespace changes](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5423/changes?w=1)

Fixes #5422

## Summary

- Tie store mutation keys directly to their corresponding state value types.
- Propagate the same guarantee through React store synchronization and setter helpers.
- Tighten popup interaction state syncing and replace broad `Partial<State>` accumulators with exact batched updates.
- Fix invalid call sites exposed by the stricter types and add compile-time regressions.

## Root cause

`Store.set` and several `ReactStore` helpers accepted `keyof State` independently from the generic value type. TypeScript could therefore infer the value without checking it against the selected key. `Store.update` and `useSyncedValues` accepted `Partial<State>`, which allows explicitly assigning `undefined` to required fields when `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is disabled.

Those signatures let the runtime store violate its declared state shape while selectors and component code continued to trust that shape.

Reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ghcgqkny

## Changes

- `Store.set` now accepts `State[Key]`, and `Store.update` accepts an inferred `Pick<State, Key>`.
- React store synchronization, controlled-prop, and setter helpers preserve the same key/value relationship.
- `usePopupInteractionProps` requires the common popup prop bags while validating component-specific state fields.
- Narrow floating-root synchronization to the popup-store capabilities it actually uses, preserving concrete state inference for specialized stores such as Tooltip.
- Popup, floating, and toast update paths now form exact updates while preserving batching and omitted-value behavior.
- Invalid call sites uncovered by the new types were corrected, including preventing Combobox event `type` metadata from being [merged into store state](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5423/changes#diff-30162b665077add067eff43f55765445b8292160513621f81fc186b6af941616R514-R525).
- Type-only tests cover wrong values, unknown keys, explicit `undefined`, state setters, popup interaction props, and popup open-change extra state.
- Direct tests cover the popup open-state branches that preserve active trigger data and control deferred unmounting.

## Impact

This is a breaking type change for `@base-ui/utils` consumers that pass a broad `Partial<State>` variable to `Store.update` or `ReactStore.useSyncedValues`. Existing valid object literals and exact known subsets continue to infer normally.

To migrate, represent broad partials as an exact known subset before writing them to the store. This prevents explicit `undefined` or unknown values from entering required state fields.

Store constructor initial-state parameters that still accept `Partial<State>` are deliberately out of scope for this PR and can be tightened separately.

## Validation

- `pnpm typescript`
- `pnpm eslint`
- `pnpm prettier`
- `pnpm test:jsdom ReactStore --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom popupStoreUtils --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom toast/store --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom ComboboxRootContext --no-watch`
- Focused jsdom suites for Combobox, Menu/Submenu, Tooltip, Preview Card, Popover, Dialog, Toast, and floating root synchronization

In the above example, if I provide `isItemEqualToValue={(item, value) => item.id === value}`:
- Initial highlight starts working correctly
- Selected item is no longer works correctly
- TS thinks `item` and `value` are both strings, so it errors on `item.id`

---

## Current approaches

Consider a simple object shape like
```ts
interface User {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  role: string;
  email: string;
  avatarUrl: string;
}
```

If providing just IDs as items, I need to build or look up a user object here to display all the info:

```jsx
<Combobox.Root items={userIds} value={currentUserId} onValueChange={userId => ... }>
  <Combobox.List>
    {(userId) => (
      <Combobox.Item value={userId}>
       {/* Need to build or look up the user object to use its fields */}
      </Combobox.Item>
     )}
  </Combobox.List>
</Combobox.Root>
```

If providing the entire object as item value, I need to either do a lookup in the object array to set the Root value, or to assemble this object on the fly (potentially unnecessary, would also have to deal with object equality)

```jsx
// Need to build or look up `currentUser`
<Combobox.Root items={users} value={currentUser} onValueChange={user => ... }>
  <Combobox.List>
    {(user) => (
      <Combobox.Item value={user}>
        ...
      </Combobox.Item>
     )}
  </Combobox.List>
</Combobox.Root>
```

Both examples above look simple but in real product with grouping and custom filtering complexity snowballs a lot

This would have been ideal

```jsx
<Combobox.Root items={users} value={currentUserId} onValueChange={userId => ... }>
  <Combobox.List>
    {(user) => (
      <Combobox.Item value={user.id}>
        ...
      </Combobox.Item>
     )}
  </Combobox.List>
</Combobox.Root>
```

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4951.

A store created via `createHandle` outlives the `Root` that mounts it. When a `Root` unmounted while the popup was open (for example, by navigating away), the open-cycle state (`open`/`mounted`/active trigger, plus store-specific metadata such as the open reason and transition type) stayed in the handle-owned store. When a new `Root` later adopted the same handle (navigating back), it inherited that stale state — leaving the popup stuck open, or rendering no popup while still locking the page.

This makes adopting a handle-owned store behave like creating an internal store (which is recreated on each `Root` mount): when a new `Root` adopts the handle, the open-cycle state is reset to that `Root`'s initial state. Nothing is reset on unmount itself — state written while no `Root` is mounted (e.g. by a pending hover timer) is also cleared on the next adoption.

## Details

- Adds a shared `useAdoptedStoreReset` hook in `utils/popups`, used by `usePopupStore` (Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Preview Card) and by `MenuStore.useStore` (which bypasses `usePopupStore`).
- The reset replaces the state object directly during the adopting `Root`'s render, so the `Root` and its children never render the stale open state — a reset performed in a layout effect was tried first and produced a transient mount of the stale-open popup followed by a visible close transition, because effects registered after the reset write their stale render-computed values (such as `mounted`) back into the store.
- The replacement is idempotent and re-runs on every render until the adoption commits, so a render discarded by React (StrictMode double render, interrupted/suspended render) neither loses the reset nor consumes it prematurely. Subscribers (e.g. detached triggers that stay mounted) are notified once, in a layout effect after the adoption commits.
- Resetting to the `Root`'s initial state (rather than a hardcoded closed state) keeps `defaultOpen` intact; the controlled `open`/`triggerId` props are re-applied via `useControlledProp`.
- Beyond the base open-cycle fields (`open`/`mounted`/`transitionStatus`/active trigger/`payload`/`preventUnmountingOnClose`), each concrete store passes its own open-cycle metadata to reset through an `ADOPTION_RESET_STATE` object (the hook's `additionalResetState` argument). These are fields read during the adopting `Root`'s first render, or only re-derived by a later layout effect, so an initially open adoption (`defaultOpen` or controlled `open`) does not commit once with the previous open cycle's values:
  - **Dialog / Drawer / Alert Dialog:** `openMethod`, `nestedOpenDialogCount`, `nestedOpenDrawerCount`
  - **Popover:** `openMethod`, `openChangeReason`, `instantType`, `stickIfOpen`
  - **Tooltip:** `openChangeReason`, `instantType`, `isInstantPhase`
  - **Preview Card:** `instantType`
  - **Menu:** `activeIndex`, `allowMouseEnter`, `hoverEnabled`, `openChangeReason`, `instantType`, `stickIfOpen`, `openMethod`

  A reminder on `PopupStoreState` documents that any new open-cycle state must either be added to the reset or be re-derived by a `Root` effect.
- Popover's `Root` now disposes the timer on the store it actually uses (`store.disposeEffect()` rather than only the internal store), so a pending patient-click (`stickIfOpen`) timer scheduled on a handle-owned store is cleared when the `Root` unmounts and cannot fire into the next adoption.
- Trigger registrations are untouched; active-trigger fields are reset and re-derived from the still-mounted triggers.

## Testing

Regression tests added for all five handle-capable components, under a shared "resetting handle-owned state when a new Root adopts the handle" suite:

- **Dialog:** uncontrolled remount; controlled remount asserting no transient close cycle (via `onOpenChangeComplete`); `defaultOpen` preserved across the remount; a still-mounted detached trigger notified on adoption (StrictMode); a parent holding `open=true` across the remount; and a render-phase probe that the adopting `Root` never reads a stale nested dialog/drawer count (`it.each(['dialog', 'drawer'])`).
- **Popover:** uncontrolled remount; a hover timer firing while no `Root` is mounted; the patient-click (`stickIfOpen`) timer being cleared on unmount; and (Chromium-only) a `defaultOpen` modal `Root` locking scroll after adopting a hover-opened handle, guarding the `openChangeReason` reset.
- **Menu:** uncontrolled remount; the previously highlighted item not being restored after a remount; and a render-phase probe that a `defaultOpen` adopting `Root` never reads stale `hoverEnabled`/`openMethod`/`stickIfOpen`/`instantType`/`openChangeReason`.
- **Tooltip:** uncontrolled remount, and a render-phase probe that a `defaultOpen` adopting `Root` never reads a stale `isInstantPhase`/`instantType`.
- **Preview Card:** uncontrolled remount.

The new tests fail without the fix; the `defaultOpen` and parent-held `open=true` cases guard the fix's preservation behavior rather than the original bug. `pnpm typescript`, `pnpm eslint`, and `pnpm prettier` pass. The full Dialog/Popover/Tooltip/Preview Card/Menu suites pass in jsdom, and all `detached-triggers` suites pass in Chromium.

items.body:
Part of the Codex sweep. Ports the Select autofill and selected-state fixes (#4934) to Combobox, with the review findings from that port folded in.

## Changes

- Browser autofill matches an item's rendered label, not just its serialized value, so a primitive `value="US">United States` autofills correctly. Works for inline children and the `items` prop.
- Field state (dirty, validation, error clearing) runs through the shared `useValueChanged` effects and respects `onValueChange`/`onInputValueChange` cancellation. A canceled autofill, selection, or input change no longer touches field state, and a canceled single selection keeps the popup open.
- Multiple mode clears `data-dirty` when the value returns to its initial set, comparing element-by-element with the item comparator instead of by array reference.
- When the input is inside the popup, the trigger's `aria-controls` points at the dialog popup (a stable `${rootId}-popup` id shared by the popup and trigger) instead of the listbox.
- `Combobox.Label` resolves to `Combobox.Label.State` in the generated docs.

## Original findings addressed

- Canceling a single-select item press still closed the popup; it now stays open, with a test.
- The `${rootId}-popup` id was built in both the popup and the trigger; it's now one `getComboboxPopupId` helper, with the custom-id path covered.
- The autofill `forceMounted` mount was sticky and ran for `multiple` and `none` modes that never match; it's now scoped to single-selection autofill.

items.body:
# Get help
Summary


Base UI Input (which renders Field.Control) triggers React state updates on each keystroke (setDirty, setFilled), causing the input component/subtree to re-render continuously while typing. This happens even when the input is used in an uncontrolled way via React Hook Form register.

This makes Base UI Input hard to use in performance-sensitive forms, because RHF’s usual “uncontrolled input = minimal rerenders” benefit is lost.

Expected behavior


When using an uncontrolled input (no value prop, only ref/onChange/onBlur from RHF register), typing should not force React re-renders of the input subtree on every keystroke unless the consumer explicitly opts into controlled state or subscriptions.

Actual behavior


Typing into Base UI Input triggers re-renders on every keystroke.

## Ask a question

Request / questions

1. Is there an intended way to use Base UI Input in a mode that avoids per-keystroke React state updates (and therefore avoids re-rendering the control)?

2. Would you consider an opt-out for tracking dirty/filled/focused state (e.g. trackDirty, trackFilled, trackFocus) for integrations where an external form library owns state/validation?

3. Alternatively, could Field.Control avoid updating React state on each input event and instead update some of this state on blur/commit, or compute it from DOM without setting state?

# Bug report

## Current behavior

`Field` does not validate the initial value and the validation is inconsistent and incorrect.

With this code:

```tsx
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Field.Control type="email" defaultValue="not_an_email@" />
</Field.Root>
```

# PR review

Root cause analysis is correct and the fix works — I reproduced the bug on master with Select (stuck `data-dirty` after clearing to `null`) and RadioGroup (inverse: `data-dirty` wrongly clears when returning to the first-picked value), and both heal with this change. The affected surface is every null-initial control (NumberField, Select single, Combobox/Autocomplete single, RadioGroup with no `defaultValue`), so the scope is wider than the title suggests. Nothing merge-blocking; the main gap is test coverage for the other affected components.

## Bugs (2)

### 1. 🟡 `ranOnce` never resets when the control unregisters

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/field-register-control/useFieldControlRegistration.ts:33`

```tsx
const ranOnce = React.useRef(false);
```

The flag lives on the Field root and is never cleared, including in the `register(source, undefined)` unregister path. If a null-initial control (e.g. NumberField) mounts first and is later swapped for a different control with a `defaultValue` under the same `Field.Root`, the second control's initial value is never captured, so its dirty state is computed against the first control's `null` baseline.

**Failure scenario:** Field conditionally renders NumberField, then swaps to a text input with `defaultValue="x"` — the input shows `data-dirty` immediately without user interaction.

**Fix:** Reset `ranOnce.current = false` in the unregister branch of `register` (where `registrationRef.current = null` is set).

### 2. ℹ️ Behavior change for late-arriving controlled values

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/field-register-control/useFieldControlRegistration.ts:86`

Previously, a controlled null-initial control whose value arrives asynchronously (e.g. Select `value` set after a fetch) had that first non-null value recorded as the baseline, so it was not dirty. With this fix the baseline stays `null`, so the field becomes `data-dirty` with no user interaction. Arguably the new behavior is the correct reading of "changed since mount", but it is an observable change worth deciding intentionally rather than by accident.

## Tests (1)

### 1. 🟠 Only NumberField is pinned; the other affected controls have no regression test

**Location:** `packages/react/src/field/root/FieldRoot.test.tsx:1470`

The fix is in a shared util, and the two failure modes are distinct: stuck-dirty (NumberField, Select single, Combobox single) and dirty-wrongly-cleared (RadioGroup: pick A, pick B, return to A — must stay dirty since the true initial was `null`). The new test pins only the first mode via NumberField. Existing `[data-dirty]` tests for Select single, Combobox, and Autocomplete are one-way (assert dirty appears, never return to initial), and RadioGroup has no positive dirty test at all, so a future regression in either mode would ship silently for those components.

**Fix:** Add one test per failure mode — a Select (or Combobox) clear-to-null round-trip, and the RadioGroup return-to-first-pick case.

## Simplifications (1)

### 1. 🟡 Ref naming convention

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/field-register-control/useFieldControlRegistration.ts:33`

Refs in this file follow the `xxxRef` suffix (`registrationRef`, `markedDirtyRef`, `activeFieldControlSourceRef`). Rename `ranOnce` to something like `syncedInitialValueRef` — also self-documents what ran once.

## Docs (1)

### 1. ℹ️ Title/commit scope undersells the fix

The change fixes Select, Combobox/Autocomplete, and RadioGroup dirty tracking too, not just NumberField. Suggest retitling to `[field] Fix data-dirty tracking for null-valued controls` so the changelog reaches affected users.

## Verdict

**Approve after nits** — fix is verified correct across all affected components; missing regression tests for Select/RadioGroup are the main gap.

🤖 Review generated with Claude Code

>1. 🟡 ranOnce never resets when the control unregisters

Fixed this bug but in different way than suggested. Suggested way reintroduced initial bug which this PR intended to fix

>2. ℹ️ Behavior change for late-arriving controlled values

I think new behaviour is correct, dirty means the value differs from the initial value captured at mount, so a value that arrives later (async fetch / setValue) is a change → dirty. If a fetched value should be the baseline, set it as the field's initial value (render it from the start or reset the form).

>Only NumberField is pinned; the other affected controls have no regression test

Fixed

>Ref naming convention

Fixed

>Title/commit scope undersells the fix

Fixed

>New agent review, keep finding fresh issues - this one is narrow, though

Fixed, hopefully everything is resolved now :)

They kept finding new issues :-) 

A remount and a control swap look identical to the registration hook (both are unregister -> register with all-new identity), and each fix guessed with a different proxy, so each one fixed one case and broke another. 

The new guard (I pushed above) uses the only signal that actually separates them: a new instance registering with the previous instance's last known value is a remount (keep baseline), anything else is a swap (recapture). This is independent of dirty history, so `validate()`/user edits can't poison a later swap.

Will re-review with both 5.6 + Fable now

It turns out the first review's bug was something that should have been ignored.

The original review assumed swapping controls inside the same `<Field.Root>` should reset its baseline. Trying to preserve remounts while supporting that behavior led to unreliable source/value heuristics and several follow-up fixes. I ultimately realized that the baseline belongs to `<Field.Root>`, so the original capture-once approach was correct

The first reported bug was a non-issue because swapping a control does not create a new field: the baseline belongs to the Field root. The reported immediate `data-dirty` issue also does not occur, since registration does not recompute dirty state on mount. A new baseline requires remounting or keying the Field root.

React bails out if it's the same value `onChange`, so it doesn't cause a re-render until the input value returns to the initial value. So for an initially empty input, `filled`/`dirty` change together (batched re-render) and no extra re-renders occur while typing afterwards until the input is cleared again

With #3820, a re-render occurs once when focusing the control (`focused` state), and then again once on the first keystroke, but not any point after that, for an initially empty input
This re-renders of focus and first typing are acceptable or negligible.
